checks_run.note: All tests pass, including the four new firstmate-study tests and xtask policy tests (non-Rust inventory, boundary scan). The tree-bound tests ran against pinned-source/.

open_issues: The two tree-bound tests return early where pinned-source/ is absent (a plain checkout or CI), so they check nothing there. They are real only where the mount exists, as in a study job.
The pin SHA was taken from the request and could not be checked against git history. D78 says so.
No run of firstmate: every claim is marked read, and the failure/retry edges t2, t5, t7 and t8 carry a could-not-run finding.
The enforcement tag lives in claim text because study.claim/1 has no field for it.
The model is small (5 states, 8 transitions). It does not cover scouts, secondmates, away mode or the PR-merge scripts.
mistakes: Cited fm-backlog-transition-lib.sh line 46 for a quote that is on line 45; the new test failed on it and I fixed it.
First wrote the inventory row as `studies/**/*.json`, which the xtask matcher does not understand; changed to `studies/**` before running xtask tests.
learnings: pinned-source/ has no git metadata and no SHA file, so the pin SHA can only come from the request; a test cannot confirm it names a commit.
xtask's inventory matcher only understands `dir/**`, `*.ext`, exact paths and bare names. A row such as `studies/**/*.json` would not match, so the row is `studies/**`.
study.claim/1 has no field for 'mechanism or prose-only'. The tag is the first words of the claim text.
EvaluatedBy has no 'nobody' value, so a guard of none has to carry some value in guard_evaluated_by.
The rules need findings (unexercised-path), and the deliverable list has no findings file, so I added findings.json.
Quote lines containing the forbidden boundary words (the pinned tree uses them often) were avoided by picking other lines.
Pinned line numbers drift easily: my first draft cited line 46 where the quote is on 45. The kept test caught it.
desires: A way to read the pinned commit id from the job record, so the test would not hard-code it.
Permission to run the studied system under a recorded boundary, so some claims could be marked observed.
